subject: Invoicing aggregation & tax entity routing for ACME order form
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme-software.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acme-software.com
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Invoicing aggregation & tax entity routing for ACME order form

Hi Jasmine / Camila,

Thanks again for the demo last week — ACME is ready to move forward but Procurement raised a few operational questions before we can sign the order form. High level: we have two legal entities (ACME US and ACME EMEA) and want invoices to be routed to each entity based on the product lines, but we'd prefer to receive a consolidated monthly invoice for reconciliation if possible. Specific asks:

- Can Redwood issue one consolidated invoice per calendar month but include line-level entity routing so we can apply the correct VAT/company codes?
- How will minimum commits be represented on the invoice(s) if the commit spans multiple entities?
- ACME generally requires Net 30. Does Redwood have flexibility on net terms or volume-based credit for Net 30?
- We need VAT evidence for EMEA — can you provide standard VAT certificates or a playbook for tax handling?

I attached our PO and the procurement checklist.

Attachments: ACME_PO_2026.pdf (application/pdf)

Appreciate a quick note on feasibility and the expected day-to-day invoicing flow. If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min call this week.

Best,
Sarah Liu
Senior Procurement Manager
ACME Software

---

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme-software.com>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Invoicing aggregation & tax entity routing for ACME order form

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear summary and the PO. We can support the consolidated invoice + line-level entity breakdown you described, but there are a few tradeoffs to flag so we can align with Finance and Legal. Proposed approach:

- Invoicing cadence: one consolidated invoice per calendar month (single document) with line items tagged to your entity codes. We will include the entity identifier in the invoice line description so your AP can split entries to each legal entity.
- Minimum commit: we propose showing the committed quantity and the month-to-date consumption on the consolidated invoice; any shortfall true-up would be invoiced monthly until the commit period ends. If you need separate legal invoices per entity, we can do that but it will increase operational overhead and may change the billing entity on the invoice (requires legal review).
- Net terms: standard Redwood hosted terms are Net 45; for Net 30 we can explore a small prepayment or a volume-based credit that offsets the earlier payment requirement. I'll loop in Ben (Finance) and Steph (Legal) to confirm.
- VAT/evidence: we can provide VAT registration evidence and a short playbook for when VAT is charged vs reverse-charged. Legal will include language in the order form to capture tax responsibility and evidence requirements.

I've attached a short payment-routing proposal document for Finance to review. Can Ben and Steph please weigh in on operational/contract impact? Sarah — would a short call tomorrow (10am PT) work to finalize high-level choices?

Attachments: payment-routing-proposal.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0122

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Invoicing aggregation & tax entity routing for ACME order form

Thanks — practical comments from Finance below. Quoting Jasmine's summary for context.

Key points:
- Consolidated monthly invoice with line-level entity tags: OK from a systems standpoint, but we need a reliable field (entity code) on each line so our AP automation can ingest and route. That means the order form needs an appendix listing entity codes and mapping rules.
- Minimum commit handling: prefer monthly true-ups as Jasmine proposed. We should avoid creating separate "committed invoices" per entity; instead show the committed allocation per entity on the consolidated invoice and true-up shortfalls monthly.
- Net terms: we can offer Net 30 for this deal with a 1.5% service fee applied to the invoice if paid after Net 30 but before Net 45, OR we can trade Net 30 for a 2% prepay credit on first quarter invoicing. Pick one approach and we can reflect in the order form.
- VAT evidence: Finance needs a specific attach-and-store flow. If ACME can supply VAT certs per entity at signing, we'll store them and apply the routing. Otherwise, Redwood legal will need a clause requiring receipt of VAT evidence within X days of first invoice for EMEA.

Action items for internal:
- Steph: please redline the order form to include a line-level entity mapping appendix, an invoice acceptance period (10 business days), and the VAT evidence requirement.
- Jasmine / Camila: confirm which of the Net 30 options ACME prefers (1.5% service fee vs 2% prepay credit).

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

---

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme-software.com>, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Invoicing aggregation & tax entity routing for ACME order form

Sarah / team — attaching a redline of the draft order form with proposed language to support the consolidated invoice + entity mapping. Summary of legal changes:

- Section 2.1 (Billing): Add a new Appendix A (Entity Mapping) referenced on the invoice. Redwood will include a line-level "EntityCode" field and the consolidated invoice will contain an "Entity Allocation" column.
- Section 3.4 (Commitments & True-up): Commitments will be shown as allocation percentages per entity; shortfalls will be invoiced monthly.
- Section 5.2 (Payment Terms): We can accept Net 30 with the commercial compromise Ben proposed (1.5% service fee for Net 30 vs Net 45), or Net 30 in exchange for a 2% prepayment credit on the first quarter. Please confirm which commercial option you prefer and we'll insert the correct clause.
- Section 7.1 (Taxes): Add requirement that customer provide VAT registration evidence for each EMEA entity within 15 days of first invoice; failure to provide evidence will result in Redwood applying local VAT until evidence is received.
- PO & Invoice acceptance: Add an invoice acceptance window of 10 business days; disputes must be raised within this window or invoice will be deemed accepted.

Attachments: redline_orderform_ACME.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)
Related: DocuSign envelope https://docusign.com/AA1b2c3d4e5f6

I've tried to keep language narrow to minimize legal tail. If ACME prefers separate legal invoices instead of consolidated with mapping, that will require changing the billing entity in Section 1 and we should treat that as a different order form.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Commercials
Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai

From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme-software.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, procurement@acme-software.com
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Invoicing aggregation & tax entity routing for ACME order form

Thanks, everyone — the redline looks reasonable and I appreciate the clarity. A few quick points from Procurement:

- ACME prefers Net 30 with the 2% prepayment credit on first quarter (we can align finance for that). Please insert that option into the payment terms.
- Appendix A entity mapping is fine — we'll provide the entity codes and VAT certs for ACME US and ACME EMEA at signing.
- Invoice acceptance: we agree to the 10 business day dispute window.

Let's go ahead with Steph's redline + Ben's Net 30 (2% prepayment credit) path. Happy to sign once the revised order form is sent over. If you want to send a final order form for signature, send via DocuSign and we'll route it to our legal/procurement.

Thanks,
Sarah Liu
Senior Procurement Manager
ACME Software
